key_insight: A mixed finite element formulation couples concentration, temperature, and flow to model heat-assisted consolidation and sedimentation.
engineering_relevance: The model supports simulation of thermally assisted settling of mineral suspensions, linking heat transport to solids concentration and fluid motion.
method: Use a quasi-stationary mixed formulation with pseudostress and temperature/concentration gradient variables.
Establish continuous well-posedness using Babuška–Brezzi theory and Banach’s fixed-point theorem.
Develop finite element discretizations with discrete existence, Céa-type estimates, and a priori error bounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical examples demonstrate model performance and confirm theoretical convergence rates; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: Continuous existence and uniqueness require small-data assumptions and additional solution regularity.
paper_title: Mixed finite element methods for a heat-assisted model of sedimentation
